newsitem.title: USA: Treasury seeks to give index note sale date soon.
newsitem.headline: Treasury seeks to give index note sale date soon.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Deputy Assistant Secretary for Federal Finance Roger Anderson said he would like to announce the date of the first inflation-indexed note auction later this week.
When asked by a reporter in New York about disclosing possible auction dates, Anderson replied: "I would like to do it this week."
Anderson noted that back in September, the Treasury Department had projected a January 15, 1997 issuance date. However, he added: "We haven't decided finally."
As for when the January note issue may settle, Anderson said the Treasury was still contemplating delaying the settlement date.

"If we were to delay the settlement by a week -- and yes, it is still under consideration -- the settlement would be with a week's worth of accrued interest and a week's worth of inflation adjustment," he said.
Anderson also said the creation of a liquid retail market would not be immediate.
"We expect that the retail market is going to take some time to develop," he said. "Individuals move more slowly in their investment decisions than institutions."
